{{AnimeLocationInfobox |name=Forest of Okoya |image=Forest of Okoya.png |imagesize=300px |characters=オコヤの森 |japanese=Forest of Okoya |region=Unknown |colorscheme=Galar |epicode=M23 |episode=Secrets of the Jungle }} The '''Forest of Okoya''' (Japanese: '''オコヤの{{ruby|森|もり}}''' ''Forest of Okoya'') is an {{pkmn|animated series}}-exclusive location and one of the settings for ''[[M23|Secrets of the Jungle]]''. ==History== The Forest of Okoya, which bordered [[Milyfa Town]], was home to a great many varieties of Pokémon including those that normally wouldn't be found in a forest like {{p|Flygon}}. However the forest was also the home to a group of {{p|Zarude}} that would go about intimidating the other Pokémon and stealing their food. It was rumoured that a {{p|Celebi}} previously lived in the forest too but hadn't been seen for many many years. It was also said that Celebi had brought an {{pkmn|Egg}} back from the future. Hidden in the forest was a giant tree which housed a spring where the Zarude lived. The water had amazing healing properties, rapidly repairing many injuries and illnesses in seconds. This caused it to be brought to the attention of the Biotope Company, which focused on therapeutic springs, where it was researched by the Company's leaders [[Chrom and Phossa Molybdenum]]. Although they found the spring, they learned how it was revered by the Zarude and decided to suspend the project of harvesting the water and its properties until they could find a way to do so without destroying the tree and the Zarude who lived there. Unfortunately, one of their scientists, [[Doctor Zed]], was determined to deliver the healing properties of the water to the public and refuses to let a single group of Pokémon stand in his way. He tried to forcibly take the research, however Chrom and Phossa fled with their infant son [[Koko (M23)|Al]]. Doctor Zed ran them off the road and left them to die in the ensuing explosion, not realizing the couple's final act was to send Al to safety down the river. Al was found by a single [[Dada|Zarude]] who raised him as a son in the jungle and named him Koko. ==Trivia== * Forest of Okoya was used as the [[Original Trainer|OT]] of Japanese {{p|Zarude}}, Japanese [[Dada]] Zarude, and Japanese {{Shiny}} {{p|Celebi}} event distribution for {{g|Sword and Shield}}, a reference to the twenty-third movie Zarude, Dada Zarude, and Shiny Celebi in Forest of Okoya. ===Origin=== {{main|Pokémon world in relation to the real world#In the movies|Pokémon world in relation to the real world → In the movies}} The Forest of Okoya is likely based on the {{wp|Daintree Rainforest}} in the {{wp|Wet Tropics of Queensland}} in northeastern {{wp|Australia}}, where the site is considered as the world's oldest continuously surviving tropical rainforest. Director Tetsuo Yajima had revealed that the production team went to {{wp|Cairns}} in search for its junglesEpisode 2 of Pocket Monsters the Movie "Koko" Supporters' Podcast - "The Movie Secrets We Want to Tell You" on the Pokémon movie website ([https://web.archive.org/web/20201225195748/https://www.pokemon-movie.jp/podcast/ archived]) (Japanese) ([https://dogasu.bulbagarden.net/movies/2020_pm_koko/podcast/pm_koko_podcast_episode_02.html Summary on Dogasu's Backpack]) with the Daintree Rainforest located just around a hundred kilometers north of the city. ==Names== {| class="roundtable" style="background:#{{colorschemedark|Galar}}; border:3px solid #{{locationcolor/med|forest}}" |- ! style="background:#{{colorschemelight|Galar}}" | Language ! style="background:#{{colorschemelight|Galar}}" | Name ! style="background:#{{colorschemelight|Galar}}" | Origin |- | Japanese | オコヤの森 ''Okoya no Mori'' | From 親子 ''oyako'' (parent and child) |- | English | Forest of Okoya | rowspan="5" | Transcription of its Japanese name |- | German | Okoya-Wald |- | European Spanish,
